deadline.value: Applications received by January 15 get full consideration; most offers go out by April 15. The fee waiver window closes December 13.
deadline.quote: Applications received by Jan. 15 are given full consideration and the majority of offers are made by April 15.

app_fee.value: Physics charges $55 USD for international applicants.
app_fee.quote: The Application fee is $50 for domestic applicants and $55 for international applicants.

fee_waiver.value: Physics may waive the fee for PhD applicants with a GPA above 3.7 who meet the English rules and apply by December 13.
fee_waiver.quote: The application fee waiver can be considered for applications to the Ph.D. program that satisfy a GPA greater than 3.7 and the minimum English proficiency requirements (see above) and submitted on or before Dec. 13.

gre_general.value: The General GRE is optional for physics applicants.
gre_general.quote: The Verbal and Quantitative GRE General Tests are optional.

gre_subject.value: The Physics GRE Subject Test is optional.
gre_subject.quote: The Physics GRE Subject Test is optional.

toefl_min.value: Physics requires a TOEFL iBT of 95 (or 590 on the paper test).
toefl_min.quote: The minimum scores for Physics and Astronomy are TOEFL are 95 (iBT) or 590 (PBT)

ielts_min.value: Physics requires an IELTS score of 7 across all bands.
ielts_min.quote: for the IELTS a minimum score of 7 across all bands is required

supervisor.value: Admission is decided by the department's Admissions Committee; a research advisor is chosen after the first-year evaluation.
supervisor.quote: The Admissions Committee in the Physics & Astronomy Department looks for candidates with an aptitude for and active interest in scientific inquiry.

also.quote: After passing the comps, students form a Dissertation Committee in consultation with their research advisor.

funding.value: Virtually all physics graduate students are supported, usually by a teaching assistantship early on and a research assistantship later.
funding.quote: Virtually all graduate students in the Department of Physics & Astronomy are supported financially, usually via a teaching assistantship (TA) during their first one or two years and a research assistantship (RA) thereafter.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's degree is the entry requirement; a U.S. master's-equivalent degree is not needed.
entry_route.quote: Applicants are not required to hold a U.S. master's-equivalent degree for admission.

notes: The Physics PhD page lists Astrophysics and Cosmology as a concentration, so astronomy is in also_fields. The Physics TA stipend for year one is stated as $27,000 on the financial aid page.
